contributions.headingText: Epithelioid trophoblastic tumour (ETT) is a malignant neoplasm of chorionic-type intermediate trophoblast.
2C75.0 & XH8FW3 Malignant trophoblastic neoplasms of placenta & Trophoblastic tumour, epithelioid
Uterine corpus, lower uterine segment, cervix, fallopian tube, ovary, and peritoneum

Vaginal bleeding is the most common symptom. Antecedent gestations include term pregnancy in 67% cases, spontaneous abortion in 16%, and hydatidiform mole in 16%, with latency ranging from 1 to 18 years (average: 6 years) {9808132; 18580489; 25773203; 24525845}. Mildly to moderately elevated serum hCG (< 2500 mIU/mL) is detectable in 80% of cases {16258513; 18720920}.

ETT is the rarest form of gestational trophoblastic tumour, representing 0.8–2.3% of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia {21247618; 20087692}. It develops in patients aged 15–66 years (mean: 37 years) and can occur in postmenopausal women {25773203; 23970158}.

ETT arises from trophoblast with differentiation towards chorionic-type intermediate trophoblast {9808132}. Atypical placental site nodule has been proposed as the precursor lesion {23688193; 18983471; 25675185}. An absence of Y chromosome complement is seen in the majority of tumours {20182630; 27246306}, and an undisturbed genome was reported in a comparative genomic hybridization study {18820674}.

ETT forms invasive, discrete nodules or cystic haemorrhagic masses with a cut surface that is whitish-tan to brown in colour and shows varying amounts of haemorrhage and necrosis. Ulceration and fistula formation are common. Nearly 50% of these tumours arise in the cervix or lower uterine segment {16258513; 9808132}.

A well-circumscribed nodular proliferation of medium-sized trophoblastic cells is characteristic. Tumour cells form arrangements ranging from nests or cords to large masses. The cells are relatively uniform, with a moderate amount of finely granular eosinophilic to clear cytoplasm, distinct cell membranes, and round nuclei with distinct small nucleoli. Moderate nuclear atypia is generally present, and the mitotic count varies widely. Some cases lack mitotic activity. Extensive or geographical necrosis is common. Eosinophilic hyaline-like material is characteristically present in the centre of tumour nests or between tumour cells {16258513; 9808132; 11192071}. Decidualized stromal cells may be found at the tumour periphery. When involving the cervix, the tumour cells may colonize the mucosal epithelium, simulating high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion {16258513}.

The tumour cells diffusely express HSD3B1, HLA-G, p63, cyclin E, α-inhibin, and GATA3. Scattered cells express MCAM and hPL, and the Ki-67 proliferation index is > 10% {17498600; 21588865}.

The differential diagnoses include choriocarcinoma (particularly after chemotherapy), placental site trophoblastic tumour, and cervical squamous cell carcinoma {26630228; 16258513}. ETT may be part of a mixed trophoblastic tumour {12823059; 29897391}.

Cytological smears may show clusters of slightly discohesive mononuclear tumour cells with irregularly enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, one or two inconspicuous nucleoli, and abundant vacuolated cytoplasm {11940211; 24525845}.
DNA genotyping provides a definitive diagnostic separation of ETT from somatic carcinoma {18820674; 26980014} and may be helpful.
Essential: a nodular lesion with destructive growth, consisting of epithelioid intermediate trophoblastic cells; in some cases, a Ki-67 proliferation index of > 10% is important for diagnosis.
The FIGO and Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM classifications are used for staging.

Metastasis occurs in 25–30% of cases, and patients die of disease in 10–24% of cases {25773203; 27743739; 28217684}. High mitotic count and an interval of > 4 years since antecedent pregnancy may portend a worse prognosis {20739008; 25773203}. PDL1 is highly expressed in ETT {27362903; 31013360; 30339966; 29185430}. The FIGO risk scoring system is not recommended for guiding treatment {27743739}.
